thread:
nora: FYI, noticed a steady RSS climb in the canary for the streaming tool-loop test. ~1.1GB over 4h, no obvious spike when requests arrive. seems tied to long contexts.
sam: Can you paste the basic repro and any quick heap stats?
nora: Repro: run tools/longchat_loop.sh --iter 1000 --keep-alive, uses prefix-cache + tool calls. Attached a small snapshot from top/mem: 
```
PID USER      PR  NI    VIRT    RES    SHR S  %CPU %MEM     TIME+ COMMAND
8421 redwood   20   0 21.3G 7.8G  324M S   45.3 12.5   3:14.33 runtime_worker
```
And /proc/<pid>/smaps shows many anon huge regions under kv_cache_mapped.
lee: Interesting. Any change after we flipped eviction_policy to adaptive-clock yesterday?
nora: The canary was on adaptive-clock. I rolled an older config with lru for comparison — the climb still present but slower.
priya: Do we have perf/maps + heap profiles around the 2h mark? Even a flamegraph helps.
mike: I grabbed a pstack+perf top around 2h: a bunch of allocations coming from kv_page_alloc and slab_grow paths. Suspect fragmentation: pages allocated but never reused because pin refs aren't dropping.
priya: Can you paste the perf sample snippet?
mike: Sure: 
```
# sample 1000 / 10s
kv_page_alloc  63.4%
prefix_cache_get 12.0%
tool_loop_dispatch 8.5%
other 16.1%
```
sam: That kv_page_alloc percentage is suspiciously high for steady-state. Could be a missed free path on tool error returns.
lee: Another angle: are we leaking per-session KV handles that keep a strong reference to pages? I recall a change in the session pinning refactor last quarter.
nora: Good call — session pinning patch rfc/370 added an extra ref in the happy-path on tool return to avoid double-free races. Maybe it's never dropped on long-running tool loops.
priya: Can we add an extra metric: kv_pinned_count by session_id and emit on the canary? If pinned count per session monotonically rises, that's our smoking gun.
mike: I instrumented that locally — pinned_count for session X goes 1 -> 2 -> 3 over time, never decreases until session termination.
priya: OK that's it. Hypothesis: ref-count bump on tool completion path not decremented on subsequent reuse, causing residency to grow.
sam: Quick mitigation: reduce pin window to zero on canary (disable keep-alive pin extension) and observe. If RSS stabilizes, use as hotfix.
nora: I pushed a test branch: refs/heads/try/kv-pin-fix-20260318 and ran the canary with KEEP_ALIVE_PIN_MS=0. After 3h the RSS delta was flat (~+30MB noise).
nora: Link to run: https://ci.internal/runs/3122 (perf-bot logged results) :thumbsup:
perf-bot: Canary run completed: baseline RSS 7.82GB -> 7.86GB after 3h (stable). Test with original pin window: 7.82GB -> 8.95GB.
lee: Nice. We'll need a proper fix: ensure decrement on tool-return codepath and add unit tests for the pin lifecycle. Also add e2e guardrails that assert pinned_count doesn't grow across N tool iterations.
priya: I'll own the patch. Plan: revert the accidental extra ref in session_pin_refactor and add an explicit ScopedPin object to guarantee RAII semantics. PR: https://git.internal/r/eng/runtime/pulls/789
mike: I'll add a perf test that runs 5000 iterations of the tool-loop for CI perf job and record kv_pinned_count metrics.
sam: Also let's update observability: add a high-cardinality tag session_id -> sample top-N leaking sessions for triage. Keep retention short.
nora: Will follow up with a short incident note in #incidents if this had any prod customer impact. For now canary looks good with the zero-pin mitigation.
priya: ETA for patch and tests: EOD tomorrow. If green, we roll to canary and then to prod on a staged rollout with metric-based rollback.
lee: 👍 assign to priya and mike for rollout. I'll review the PR and perf numbers.
priya: Assigned, will update thread with PR link and CI logs when ready.
mike: Added a small debugger snippet to reproduce the leak locally: 
```
# repro
python tooling/run_tool_loop.py --session-id leak-debug --iterations 2000 --profile=kv_pins
```
nora: Thanks everyone. Closing loose loop once PRs merge. :wave:
